standardsBasis: Program-design target per expansion-plan-2026-09 §3 B1 (no WA K-8 world-language benchmark exists; ACTFL-anchored). Standard tags use WA's 2015 World Languages standard numbers (5 Cs). Sub-standard numbering verified 2026-09-05 against the primary source (OSPI v1.3 PDF, p.6, "II. World Languages Learning Standards"): 1.1 Interpersonal/1.2 Interpretive/1.3 Presentational Communication; 2.1 Relating Cultural Practices/2.2 Relating Cultural Products to Perspectives; 3.1 Making Connections/3.2 Acquiring Information and Diverse Perspectives; 4.1 Language/4.2 Cultural Comparisons; 5.1 School and Global Communities/5.2 Lifelong Learning.
bandNotes: Oral/aural-first: every lesson is listening, song, TPR, story, and play — written Spanish appears only as environmental print, never as a literacy requirement. Lessons are short (10-15 min). 3.2 and 4.2 are intentionally not targeted at this band (too abstract for ages 5-7); all 5 Cs are still covered via 2.x, 3.1, 4.1, and 5.x weeks. Vocabulary recycles constantly in warm-ups even though each week's coreVocabulary lists only new entries.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — exchanging basic greetings and courtesies
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Hello song ('¡Hola, hola!') with puppet; children wave and echo hola/adiós.
Day 2: Morning vs. night picture sort; act out waking up (buenos días) and sleeping (buenas noches).
Day 3: Courtesy theater — puppet forgets gracias/por favor; children coach it with the magic words.
Day 4: Sí/no listening game with thumbs up/down; silly questions ('¿Es un perro?' at pictures).
Day 5: Greeting circle review — each child greets the class and the puppet, earns a wave goodbye.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — introducing oneself by name
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Name song with ball toss — 'Me llamo...' as each child catches; teacher models first.
Day 2: Puppet interview game — '¿Cómo te llamas?' asked around the circle, echo response.
Day 3: Niño/niña picture sort with class photos and storybook characters.
Day 4: Amigo/amiga pair-up — children introduce a partner ('Mi amigo se llama...') with gesture support.
Day 5: Review fiesta — greet + introduce yourself to the puppet, combining week 1 and 2 phrases.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Listening — recognizing spoken numbers 1-5
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Counting song 'Uno, dos, tres' with finger counting; slow echo then fast echo.
Day 2: Listen-and-clap — teacher says a number, children clap that many times.
Day 3: Counting objects around the room (blocks, crayons) answering '¿cuántos?'.
Day 4: Number hop — floor dots 1-5, children jump to the number they hear.
Day 5: Counting show — each child counts a small set aloud for the puppet.

weeks.actflFocus: Presentational Speaking — counting aloud to ten
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Extend the counting song to ten with big body movements per number.
Day 2: Ten-frame beanbag toss — count throws aloud as a group.
Day 3: Hide-and-count — find hidden number cards 1-10, say each one found.
Day 4: Count-up chain — around the circle, each child says the next number.
Day 5: Solo count-to-ten performance for the puppet; class cheers in Spanish.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Listening — identifying colors by name
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Color song with scarves; wave the color you hear.
Day 2: Color hunt — touch something rojo/azul/verde in the room on command.
Day 3: Story with color pictures; children call out each color as it appears.
Day 4: Color-sort game — crayons into named buckets, counting each bucket (recycles numbers).
Day 5: 'Veo veo' (I spy) with the four strongest colors plus blanco/negro.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — asking and telling favorite colors
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Add new colors to the scarf song; rainbow line-up.
Day 2: '¿De qué color es?' picture game with animals and toys.
Day 3: Favorite-color survey — each child says 'Mi color favorito es...' with a color card.
Day 4: Class color graph — count votes per color aloud (recycles numbers 1-10).
Day 5: Color parade — children dress a paper doll in their favorite colors and present it.

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Practices to Perspectives — family names and warm family greetings in Latin America
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Family finger-play song ('La familia dedo'); name each finger family member.
Day 2: Family photo share — children point and name mamá, papá, hermanos.
Day 3: Story about a Latin American family gathering; notice hugs and greetings for abuela/abuelo.
Day 4: Draw-your-family activity; teacher labels orally as children name members.
Day 5: Family show-and-tell — present your drawing: 'Mi mamá, mi papá...'.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — talking about pets you have or want
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Pet-sound guessing game — hear the animal, say its Spanish name.
Day 2: Act-like-the-animal TPR — hop like un conejo, swim like un pez.
Day 3: Story about a lost perro; children help find it by naming animals along the way.
Day 4: Pet survey — '¿Tienes una mascota?' with sí/no and animal cards; count results.
Day 5: Show-and-tell with stuffed animals — name and describe with a color word.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Listening — following a farm story with animal names
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: 'En la granja' song (Spanish Old MacDonald pattern) with animal sounds.
Day 2: Animal-sound match — Spanish animal sounds differ (¡quiquiriquí!); match sound to picture.
Day 3: Farm story listen-along; children hold up the animal they hear.
Day 4: Farm pretend-play — teacher calls animals to the 'barn' by name.
Day 5: Review romp — farm animal freeze dance; name the animal when the music stops.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Listening — identifying wild animals in a zoo adventure story
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Zoo safari song; stomp like elefantes, stretch like jirafas.
Day 2: Guess-the-animal riddles from sounds and motions.
Day 3: Zoo adventure story listen-along with picture cards.
Day 4: Build-a-zoo — place animal figures in habitats as the teacher names them.
Day 5: Animal parade — each child moves as an animal, class names it in Spanish.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Listening — pointing to body parts on command (TPR)
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: 'Cabeza, hombros, rodillas y pies' song, slow then fast.
Day 2: Simon-says style 'Simón dice' — touch la nariz, las orejas.
Day 3: Monster-drawing listen-and-draw — 'tres ojos, una boca grande' (recycles numbers/colors).
Day 4: Body-part freeze dance; teacher names a part to wiggle.
Day 5: Puppet checkup — children play doctor, naming each body part they check.

weeks.actflFocus: Presentational Speaking — leading the class in action commands
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Action song — everyone salta, corre, baila on cue.
Day 2: 'Simón dice' with action commands.
Day 3: Obstacle course narrated in Spanish — camina, salta, párate.
Day 4: Child leaders — each child gives one command for the class to follow.
Day 5: Action freeze-dance review mixing all eight commands.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — asking and answering how you feel
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Feelings faces song; make each face as it's named.
Day 2: Morning check-in circle — '¿Cómo estás?' 'Estoy feliz' with emoji cards.
Day 3: Story about a triste puppet who becomes feliz; children name feelings at each turn.
Day 4: Feelings charades — act one out, class guesses in Spanish.
Day 5: Feelings check-in becomes a daily routine; children ask each other in pairs.

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Products to Perspectives — tropical fruits of Latin America
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Fruit song with picture cards; match fruit to its color word.
Day 2: Mystery fruit bag — feel and guess, reveal and name.
Day 3: Learn about fruit stands and mercados in Latin America; taste-test day if possible (mango, piña).
Day 4: Fruit-salad craft — glue paper fruits into a bowl, naming each.
Day 5: Fruit-stand pretend play — 'Una manzana, por favor' (recycles courtesy words).

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Practices to Perspectives — everyday foods and family mealtime in Latin America
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Food song; sort breakfast/lunch/dinner pictures.
Day 2: Learn how tortillas are made; pat-the-tortilla hand rhyme.
Day 3: Story about a family meal with arroz y frijoles; notice everyone eats together.
Day 4: Play kitchen — 'serve' foods to the puppet who says tengo hambre.
Day 5: Plate craft — assemble a paper meal and name every food on it.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — expressing likes and dislikes about food
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Thumbs-up/thumbs-down game — me gusta / no me gusta with food cards.
Day 2: '¿Te gusta?' partner survey using last week's foods.
Day 3: Silly-foods story (ice cream with frijoles?) — children react with the phrases.
Day 4: Class favorite-foods graph; count votes aloud.
Day 5: Restaurant pretend play — order with quiero + por favor, react with ¡delicioso!

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Listening — dressing a character from spoken clothing names
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Getting-dressed song with motions for each clothing item.
Day 2: Dress the paper doll — children add the item they hear.
Day 3: 'What's missing?' game — clothes disappear from the board, name the missing one.
Day 4: Color + clothing combo — 'la camisa roja' matching game (recycles colors).
Day 5: Silly fashion show — describe the puppet's mixed-up outfit.

weeks.actflFocus: Connections: Making Connections — daily weather observation (science link)
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Weather song with motions (sun arms, rain fingers); look out the window and report.
Day 2: Weather-wheel craft; set today's weather in Spanish.
Day 3: Dress-for-the-weather game — pick clothing for hace frío vs. hace calor (recycles clothing).
Day 4: Weather sounds listening game — rain, wind, storm; name what you hear.
Day 5: Daily weather reporter routine begins — one child reports each day from now on.

weeks.actflFocus: Communities: School & Global Communities — sharing our Spanish with the school community
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Greatest-hits song medley from weeks 1-18.
Day 2: Review stations — colors, numbers, animals, food games.
Day 3: Rehearse a mini-performance (songs + greetings) to share with family or another class.
Day 4: Perform for an audience — buddy class, family video, or school assembly.
Day 5: Celebration circle — each child shows a favorite word or song; ¡muy bien! all around.

weeks.actflFocus: Comparisons: Language Comparisons — day names in Spanish vs. English
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Days-of-the-week chant with a clap pattern.
Day 2: Order-the-days card line-up; sing to check.
Day 3: Compare: English day names vs. Spanish (sábado starts with s like Saturday? lunes like 'lunar' moon day) — word detectives.
Day 4: 'What day is it?' calendar routine begins; mark today.
Day 5: Days relay — class chants the week while passing a ball, no drops!

weeks.actflFocus: Connections: Making Connections — the four seasons and nature's changes (science link)
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Four-seasons song with a motion per season.
Day 2: Season sort — pictures of snow, flowers, leaves, beach into season groups.
Day 3: Match weather phrases to seasons (recycles week 18).
Day 4: Four-seasons tree craft — one branch per season, name each.
Day 5: Season charades — act out a season activity, class guesses la estación.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Listening — recognizing teen numbers and ages
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Count past ten with the counting song extended; jump on each new number.
Day 2: Number-line hop 11-20; land where the teacher says.
Day 3: Age circle — '¿Cuántos años tienes?' 'Tengo seis años' with candles craft.
Day 4: Count classroom collections past ten (recycles ¿cuántos?).
Day 5: Number bingo 1-20.

weeks.actflFocus: Presentational Speaking — describing shapes by name and size
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Shape song; draw each shape in the air.
Day 2: Shape hunt around the room — find un círculo, un cuadrado.
Day 3: Big/small sort — grande vs. pequeño with real objects.
Day 4: Shape-picture craft — build an animal from paper shapes.
Day 5: Present your shape picture: 'Un círculo grande, dos triángulos pequeños...'.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Listening — locating things and rooms in a house
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: House song; touch classroom puerta/ventana/mesa/silla on cue.
Day 2: Dollhouse game — put the family member where the teacher says.
Day 3: Story set inside a house; children point to each room on a picture map.
Day 4: Draw-your-house activity; name the parts aloud.
Day 5: Hide-and-seek with a toy — '¿Está en la cocina?' sí/no guessing.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — asking for classroom items politely
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Classroom-objects song; hold up each real item as it's named.
Day 2: Pack-the-mochila game — put in only what the teacher names.
Day 3: Polite requests — 'El lápiz, por favor' 'Gracias' passing game.
Day 4: I-spy classroom edition with school objects.
Day 5: Play school — children take turns being la maestra giving commands (recycles week 12).

weeks.actflFocus: Communities: School & Global Communities — people who help us in every community
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Helpers song; hat/prop for each helper as it's named.
Day 2: Who-helps-whom matching — la veterinaria with la mascota (recycles animals).
Day 3: Story about helpers in a Spanish-speaking neighborhood.
Day 4: Dress-up dramatic play — act out each helper's job.
Day 5: 'When I grow up' share — 'Quiero ser doctora' with a drawing.

weeks.actflFocus: Presentational Speaking — presenting how you travel
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Transportation song with vehicle motions and sounds.
Day 2: Sound guessing — engine, horn, whistle; name the vehicle.
Day 3: Land/water/air sort with vehicle cards.
Day 4: Build a vehicle craft from shapes (recycles week 23).
Day 5: Present your vehicle: 'Mi carro es rojo y grande' (recycles colors/sizes).

weeks.actflFocus: Connections: Making Connections — plants, insects, and how gardens grow (science link)
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Garden song — grow from seed to flor with your whole body.
Day 2: Nature walk or window watch — spot and name árboles, hojas, insectos.
Day 3: Life-of-a-mariposa mini-story with motions.
Day 4: Plant a real seed; start saying 'agua para la planta' each day.
Day 5: Garden collage craft; present it naming each item.

weeks.actflFocus: Comparisons: Language Comparisons — playing with opposite words in two languages
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Opposites song — stretch alto, crouch bajo, hands arriba/abajo.
Day 2: Fast/slow movement game — move rápido or lento on command.
Day 3: Opposite pairs matching cards; say both words in the pair.
Day 4: Word detectives — do any Spanish opposites sound like English ones? (rápido/rapid!).
Day 5: Opposites obstacle course narrated by the class.

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Practices to Perspectives — birthday traditions: piñatas and Las Mañanitas
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Learn 'Las Mañanitas' chorus — the birthday song across Latin America.
Day 2: Party vocabulary game — decorate the pretend fiesta as items are named.
Day 3: All about piñatas — where they come from, how the game works.
Day 4: Make a mini paper piñata or party hat craft.
Day 5: Class fiesta simulation — sing, count candles, say ¡feliz cumpleaños!

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Products to Perspectives — instruments and rhythms of Latin America
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Listen to mariachi, cumbia, and salsa clips; move to each ritmo.
Day 2: Instrument sounds game — hear it, name it (la trompeta, el tambor...).
Day 3: Make shaker maracas from cups and beans.
Day 4: Class rhythm band — follow spoken directions for loud/soft, rápido/lento (recycles opposites).
Day 5: Mini concert — perform a favorite class song with homemade instruments.

weeks.actflFocus: Presentational Speaking — announcing the day and date in the calendar routine
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Calendar routine upgrade — hoy es + day; count the date aloud together.
Day 2: Hoy/mañana/ayer hop — three floor spots, jump to the one you hear.
Day 3: Count calendar days toward a class event; practice numbers 21-30.
Day 4: Month birthday graph — whose cumpleaños is this mes? (recycles week 30).
Day 5: Child-led calendar — a student announces day and date to the class.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Listening — following a fairy tale told in Spanish
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Hear the fairy tale with big pictures; learn érase una vez and el final as bookends.
Day 2: Retell with picture cards in order; children place each scene.
Day 3: Act it out — princesa, dragón, castillo roles with simple lines.
Day 4: Change the story — new animal hero? New color dragon? Class chooses.
Day 5: Story theater performance of the class version.

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Products to Perspectives — town squares and open-air markets in Latin America
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Town song; build a floor map with block buildings as each place is named.
Day 2: Photo tour of a Latin American plaza and mercado — what do you see?
Day 3: Toy-car trip around the floor map — 'al parque, a la tienda' directions.
Day 4: Set up a class mercado with fruit cards (recycles weeks 14-16).
Day 5: Mercado role-play day — buy and sell with courtesy phrases.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — kind words with friends
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Kindness song; practice perdón and gracias scenarios with the puppet.
Day 2: Sharing game — pass and share materials saying compartir phrases.
Day 3: Story about friends who solve a problem kindly; spot the kind words.
Day 4: Make a friendship card for a classmate or family member (te quiero, mi amigo).
Day 5: Deliver the cards; compliment circle — 'Eres amable' with a sonrisa.

weeks.actflFocus: Communities: Lifelong Learning — celebrating what we can do and using Spanish beyond class
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Year-in-review song medley; children pick the class favorites.
Day 2: 'I can' stations — show off counting, colors, greetings, animals (¡yo puedo!).
Day 3: Rehearse the end-of-year showcase for families.
Day 4: Showcase day — perform songs and mini-dialogues; families join the fiesta.
Day 5: Goodbye circle — certificates, ¡felicidades!, plans to keep singing in Spanish over las vacaciones.
